plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with bright colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals, surrounding small yellow true flowers. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub up to 3 meters tall, and it is also grown worldwide as a potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, grown outdoors in warm regions such as California, Florida, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants, so they need long uninterrupted nights to develop their colorful bracts. The Aztecs used them to make red dye and called them cuetlaxochitl.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It is among the earliest camellias to bloom and is popular in gardens in mild climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Australia, New Zealand, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: The leaves of the related Camellia sinensis give us tea, and sasanqua seeds are pressed for camellia oil, used in cooking and hair care in Japan.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with a umbrella-shaped canopy that becomes covered in clusters of vivid flowers, with fern-like leaves. It blooms during the Southern Hemisphere summer, creating spectacular displays in warm regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); also blooms in tropical regions from May to July
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions including Brazil, northern Australia, South Africa, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: In the wild in Madagascar it is endangered, even though it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees in the world.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery dark green leaves and cup-shaped flowers with prominent yellow stamens. It blooms in cold weather, often pushing up through snow, and it prefers partially shaded woodland conditions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and northern Apennines; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic. Legend says it sprang from the tears of a girl who had no gift for the Christ child.
